reasoning: The carve-out text at CLAUDE.md:216-221 is not a free-floating document: it is the tail of known-issue N19, anchored [:204-224] in reports/stable-staker/18/known-issues-cf8de27.md.

The re-extraction rules N19's authority explicitly and twice: line 26 'N19 - caveat STANDS, no suppression authority ... N19 evidences intent and nothing more', and sanitizer usage rule 3 'N19 suppresses nothing (unanchored self-citation)'. The carve-out justifies itself by citing a section 'idle balance is automatically buffer' that does not exist at cf8de27 - the sole occurrence of that string, at :221, IS the citation.
A known issue cannot bootstrap its own authority from a section it invents. I am not free to grant N19 the authority the KI re-extraction denied it.

Separately: even a fully-authoritative N19 would not reach the finding's actual claim. N19 asserts autoAnnihilate 'shares [the underwater path] with withdraw and does not change' it. That asserted EQUIVALENCE is exactly what this finding disputes - withdraw is a principal exit (buffer consumption is 1:1 with a position leaving), whereas autoAnnihilate is a repeatable REWARD action that stakers are steered into while claimEnabled is false, so the buffer is now drained by users who are not leaving and whose draw was never in its sizing. N19 reasons about neither frequency nor steering.
In-source NatSpec carries no suppression authority either (standing project memory); the :484-488 comment is filed separately as ss18q3 rather than credited as documentation.

findings.label: Q-02(proposed)
findings.title: The `gross` clamp is provably redundant but fails SILENTLY rather than loudly; a future refactor that breaks its premise mints free phUSD instead of reverting
findings.detail: capped <= user.amount * scale implies gross == netWanted always. But netUsed clamps against netWanted and the frictionless target is sized on netWanted, so if the premise ever breaks the contract pays a target it did not debit for - free phUSD - rather than reverting. The comment's own justification ('the debit below underflows if it is ever wrong') is backwards: the debit uses `gross`, which is the clamped value, so it cannot underflow. Recommend require(gross == netWanted).
